sources.title: Stephen A. Murphy: The case for proto-Dvaravati
sources.note: Author-uploaded full published article directly read, Journal of Southeast Asian Studies47(3),2016,pp366 to 392, DOI10.1017/S0022463416000242. SOAS accepted manuscript https://soas-repository.worktribe.com/OutputFile/413293 is a mirror of the same work, not an additional budget. Intro pp366 to 369, language/ethnicity p374, political discussion pp382 to 383. Archaeological/artistic label versus polity distinguished; Mon inscriptional evidence does not establish universal spoken ethnicity.

sources.title: U Thong National Museum: Exhibitions
sources.note: Full indexed original Fine Arts Department museum exhibition text, Glorious U Thong of Dvaravati. Elliptical plan, surrounding waterway/earthen dyke, at least20 monuments. Direct fetch fails. Modern Lao Song house and ethnography on this page are explicitly excluded from ancient household reconstruction.

sources.title: UNESCO: The Ancient Town of Si Thep and its Associated Dvaravati Monuments
sources.note: Direct official listing, Outstanding Universal Value brief synthesis and criteria: inner/outer moated town, Khao Klang Nok, Khao Thamorrat Mahayana cave monastery, Buddhist/Hindu diversity. Does not adopt promotional empire label as evidence of single political unity; no precision claim for map.

sources.title: Defining Dvaravati, edited by Anna Bennett and Hunter Watson
sources.note: DASTA/Buddhadasa Indapanno Archives,2019. John Guy, Making Sense of Dvaravati, printed54 fig7 exact Sanskrit transliteration/translation, seventh to eighth-century silver medallion found1943 near Wat Phra Paton. Exact indexed original read. Anna Bennett, Precious Metals in Dvaravati Culture, printed120 figs31 to 33 directly read in author upload https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378526667_DEFINING_DVARAVATI_Published_by_DASTA_Designated_Areas_for_Sustainable_Tourism_Administration_Public_Organization_and_BIA_Buddhadasa_Indapanno_Archives . Pool whole book/mirrors as one budget. Main PDF too large for web extraction; no visual glyph rendering claimed.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Lost Kingdoms, Dvaravati Wheels of the Law
sources.note: Official catalogue2014, printed190, fig119 and adjacent text, full indexed original checked. Pillar/socle/wheel construction, no metal pins seen and gravity interpretation; deer and first sermon symbolism. Entire book pooled under one URL. No newly invented dates or exclusive-invention superlatives.

sources.title: Kurt Behrendt: The Mon-Dvaravati Tradition of Early North-Central Thailand
sources.note: Direct2007 museum essay, clay plaques seventh to ninth centuries, artistic transmission; concluding tenth-century Khmer influence and twelfth-century SuryavarmanII invasion. Does not adopt outdated relative-isolation generalization, homogeneous ethnic equation or universal single conquest.

sources.title: Jade d’Alpoim Guedes and colleagues: Three thousand years of farming strategies in central Thailand
sources.note: Direct full2020 Antiquity94,pp966 to 982, results fig2/3 and conclusion. Phromtin Tai Dvaravati phase7 rice dominance and increase in domesticated spikelets; sampled regional sequence supports rain-fed/dryland cultivation. Do not generalize to all Dvaravati farming or prehistoric sites as contemporary communities.

sources.title: Stephen A. Murphy and Pimchanok Pongkasetkan: Fifty Years of Archaeological Research at Dong Mae Nang Muang
sources.note: Direct2010 Journal of Siam Society98,pp49 to 74. Settlement eighth to twelfth centuries; pp61 to 63 pottery, Persian turquoise-glazed ninth-century ware, grinding stones/spindle whorls/oil lamps; pp59 to 60 K966 dated1167, Khmer influence without major material-culture break. Do not reuse outdated claim no glass-bead production in centralThailand; newer UThong evidence used separately. Site extends north of imported geometry, publicly distinguished.

sources.title: Somdet Phra Narai National Museum: Terracotta figures of a mother (?) and child
sources.url: https://www.finearts.go.th/somdetphranaraimuseum/view/44156-เรื่อง--ตุ๊กตาดินเผารูป--แม่------และเด็ก--
sources.note: Direct Thai-language Fine Arts Department museum article, item1 seated woman holding child apparently feeding; alternative mother/caregiver/Hariti readings and final paragraph uncertain toy/ritual function. Catalogue dates BE12th to 16thcenturies, roughlyseventh to eleventhCE. Current museum display identified, exact excavated provenance not assigned from general list of sites. No invented medical treatment or assertion all figures are toys.

sources.title: San Thaiyanonda: Cultural development of ancient communities at Mueang U-Thong
sources.note: SilpakornUniversity2011 master thesis, Thai/English abstracts directly indexed original metadata. Study three sites excavated2010; phaseIV circa10th to 11th centuries glass-bead/metal industries, possible exports and southern-port trade. Full thesis not read; claims limited to explicit abstract.

sources.title: Fine Arts Department: The Ancient Ruins of Phu Hang Nak, Standing Stone Culture?
sources.note: Official Silpakorn journal English abstract, translated by Thanik Lertchamrit, full indexed original checked. Phu Hang Nak on Khao Rang Kapid west of UThong; monument1 excavation December2012 to March2013 and monument2 in2016; Dvaravati remains aroundninthcentury, sparse Ayutthaya reuse, no prehistoric megalith evidence. Exact printpage not recovered; English abstract uniquely located by title.
